feature: Stacked glass panes with glinting edges
what: Surfaces are drawn as sheets of dark bottle glass. Each layer up is lighter, more chromatic and a little greener (bg #051010 at h196, surface #0a1c1c, surface-2 #0f2322, surface-3 #152b29 at h188). The hairlines carry more chroma and a greener hue than the faces (line #1c3632, line-2 #284641, edge #557873), so card and bubble borders glint like the edge of a pane, and the family's bubbles become lighter teal panes.

feature: The brand is never a kind
what: Outings stop sharing the signature green. Outing gets its own colour, turquoise #43dbd0 (the light cyan of an EGA screen), so any green on an idea card or in 'Lately added' means the brand and nothing else. The rest of the kind set takes a colour monitor's phosphors, deeper and more saturated rather than pastel: ideas violet #b188fe, plans sky #6ac4fb, to do yellow #f6d94f, people #fdae4f, shows #fd82ba, seasons #fc8d5e. Every CVD distance improves (kinds 13.6 to 15.8 typical, 5.2 to 9.2 protan). Pine and Alpenglow's glacier-lake teal outing (#65d1da, round 2) is the same move.

Keep the turquoise outing and the richer sections, which are a real gain for the system." Product notes' synthesis: "08's outing with its own colour, so the brand is never a kind." Style, round 2, on Pine: "keep the glacier-teal outing, which is lovely."
caveats: In small labels only, it is invisible at a glance (feedback 5). Turquoise can read as a second blue beside trips' sky, or as more green to some eyes. The tritan pair show~seasonal fell to 5.4. The round 2 lesson says moving learned section colours costs points, so change outing and leave the sections the family knows. Switchboard: the Ideas cell's breakdown by kind. Timetable: the enamel line colours stay apart from the phosphor. Pocket: the cartridges' labels.

feature: Two inks: phosphor for the machine's voice, blue-black for the family's hand
what: One rule for colour by author. Kitchen Clock limits blue-black ink to what the family writes and touches: fields (#0b121a), date tiles and 'in N days' pills (#1b2633), their chat bubbles, links (#79a0c5) and the current tab. Cards, lines and the case stay the room's colour, and the machine's things stay green. Sonar Watch states it as 'the family's hand is ink, the machine's is phosphor', with a logbook ink (--log #141d27, --log-edge #263444, --log-ink #9eb4ca) on the family's bubbles, names, times and date leaves. Composing Room puts it in the names: 'Vera' in sage mono on her lines, the family's names in blue pencil.

feature: Family chat bubble as sewn cloth
what: The family's chat bubble is a cloth patch: a faint 45° twill texture over a solid, with a seam stitched 6px inside its edge. Vera's bubble stays smooth glass, so the two voices are told apart by material (handled cloth against lit glass) as well as by side. This matters because Chat changed least in every entrant.

suits: Pocket Timeline: the family's words as a soft sewn patch beside the machine's glass screen, tactile and toy-like. Night Timetable: the family's stops on her line set apart by material, not only by colour.

feature: Glaze: a solid lit from above that pools dark at its foot

A soft white sheen sits on the top 60% and an inset shadow pools at the foot, so the key reads as moulded and lit from above without any glow. On the phone the ways to start become chunky glazed keys.

feature: Solid tiles with no outlines, outlines returned for high contrast
what: What the family keeps is a matte solid tile with no border at all. Only a faint top-edge light and a bottom shadow separate it from the ground, so cards, panels and tabs read as objects rather than boxes, and the page loses a layer of line noise. On hover a tile lifts and gains an accent edge. Under `prefers-contrast: more` every tile gets its outline back.

feature: Grained cabinet case (rebuild as brushed metal)
what: Every monitor sits in a real-looking cabinet: a 97-degree repeating-gradient grain over a three-stop vertical gradient, a chin, a vented grille drawn as a 3rem strip of 2px bars, and a brand-green power light with a small halo. The case becomes a material object with a surface, not a grey rounded rectangle.

praise: soul 4.9: 'The walnut cabinets with grain and chin are an authentic 70s touch.' style 5.6: 'The walnut cabinets on the monitors ... are charming and have real personality.' The style notes list 'Headland Light's cabinet grain (on Sign in and 404 only)' among the seed traits worth one more try.
caveats: As wood it failed: 'kitsch' (skeptic, system, lessons.md), 'steampunk rather than period CRT' (feedback 3.2), and brown, which the owner rejects. Keep the technique, not the wood. suits: console: brushed-aluminium bays and bezels, true to a 1969 flight console, and a material that carries grounded colour without paint. switchboard: the Minitel's moulded plastic case around its terminal, a fine texture in place of the brown keys the lineage lost. pocket: the handheld's plastic shell, drawn thin, instead of the chunky beveled cartridges.

feature: Green-bar banding, rows and weeks
what: Every list the family reads (Coming up, To do, Status lights, the kids' wishes, the data tables) sits in a flat wall-less tray. Its odd rows are banded a step lighter, like the green-bar listing paper of the CRT era, so the rows drop their hairlines and pack tighter. On the Plans month, alternate weeks are banded the same way, like a printout.

The soul notes say that, tried once more, it 'belongs on slate trays, not sage ones'. lessons.md round 7: 'green-bar banding on slate trays, not sage' is worth one more try.
caveats: In sage the room read as green on green, 'more monochrome, not less' (feedback 5.2, skeptic 4.9). The bands were 'too faint to register' (style) and 'vanish on a dim screen' (interaction). Rebuild on a slate tray with a visible step of about 2.5-3 dE (for example tray #10161a and band #151c21), keep 44px rows, and use it only where rows are compared (lists, tables, the month). Do not also box each row.
suits: timetable: a printed timetable is banded, so band its timetable rows and Chat's times margin. track: the Plans month in week bands under the diagram, and Status's rows. console: Slate Flight Console already bands its rows; its month can take the week bands. switchboard: the sommaire's list of pages.

Vera's bubbles stay green-black glass (#101611) with a 30% screen edge, on a thread tray. The two speakers are two materials: the family's in a grounded solid, the machine's in glass.

feature: Warm Bakelite for the monitor case only
what: The monitors' case is drawn in one warm material, oxblood Bakelite (#3a2826, C about .025, hue 15-22). It has a warm sheen (an #ffeee6 top highlight), an inner shadow at the chin, grille slots cut into the chin and the green power LED. The case is thinner and squarer than before (padding .6rem .6rem 1.9rem, radius 18/18/22/22), with flush 14px and 8px scopes on Status and Ideas. The judges' own fix points the same way: keep the material, but use less of it.

Style's fix: "Keep the Bakelite as a frame and chrome material (bar, window frame lines, monitor case)". Skeptic's fix: "Oxblood only where there is Bakelite (the monitor case, perhaps the foot)." feature: Section-coloured band rule with a spill
what: Every section is a full-bleed band, painted by a ::before at inset 0 -100vmax, so there is no wrapper markup and no sideways scroll. Each band's top edge is a 2px rule at 70% of its section's colour, and an 8% wash of that colour fades into the band over 120px. Each page head is a lit band tinted 7% with the page's own section colour and ruled below the same way, so Plans' head reads periwinkle graphite, To do's brass and Ideas' lilac. The heading icon sits on a flat inlay cap in the section colour, applied without markup through `main h2 > svg.icon:first-child`.

feature: A round phosphor screen per page holding its one live figure
what: Each page head carries a round tube (a circular crt with a thin gauge-arc bezel and a power lamp) holding the page's one live figure in VT323: 'SPENT TODAY / $0.00 / 0% OF $2.00' on Status, 'NEXT PLAN / 17:00 / TODAY' on Plans, 'PARTS / 1 / NEED A LOOK' on Settings. The figure fills the glass by its length through container units (len-1 to len-6, 56cqi down to 26cqi). The tube's tone changes phosphor: .near turns it amber, .over red. The glass opens out of a dot when the page loads.

feature: Hatched blanking plates close any row a bank leaves open
what: Banks of equal cells run four across (two on a tablet). When the last row is short, CSS generates dashed, faintly hatched (135deg, 1px every 9px) blank plates to fill it, so the grid always reads whole, like the blanking plates in a rack or panel. Status's lamp panels, Settings' keys, Home's banks and the Plans list all use them, and the out-of-month days on the month are drawn the same way.

feature: Checkbox drawn as a lamp inside a 44px hit square
what: Each checkbox is a 44px (2.75rem) transparent square pulled back into the line with negative margins, so the row's rhythm does not move. A 1.15rem well is drawn in ::before and a clip-path tick in ::after, which scales in when ticked. The focus outline is inset by .55rem so it rings the drawn box, not the whole hit square. Home had 0 of 57 targets under 44px, and To do 0 of 97.

feature: Raised, latched and sunk control grammar
what: One affordance rule covers every control. Raised means press it: the green primary key has a 3px darker skirt and moves down 3px on :active, and the graphite secondary keys, including the band-head links 'All plans →' and 'All 4 →', have a 2px skirt. Sunk means type here: every field is a well with a darker top edge and an inset shadow. A flat inlay means it only labels: heading icon caps, date chips and initials have a 1px edge and an inner top highlight but no skirt. The mic is a round, dished arcade button.

All ten places are named, none as a bare icon, and the numbers match each page's chapter and its FIG. and plate numbers (1.2 Coming up, FIG. 1.2). feature: Separated-mosaic pictograms that could carry data
what: Every section head is led by a small drawing in separated teletext mosaic blocks: a 16x12 grid of 0.8-unit squares with gaps. It has three tones plus an accent: the section colour, a 40% dim tone for rays and glints, a whitened 'hot' block, and ochre details (the bulb's base, the calendar's rings, the bow). The drawings: a bulb with rays (Ideas), a clipboard (To do), a calendar with one block lit (Coming up), a gift (Wishes), a warning triangle (setup), a satellite dish (Status) and her monitor (Vera). crispEdges rendering and a 3px drop-shadow in the section colour make them faintly lit.

feature: Mint core, deep emerald bloom
what: Every bright core keeps today's #6dff9c, but its bloom is a deep saturated emerald (#12a472, hue 162, L 0.64) instead of a whitish mint fog. That is how a real tube blooms: darker and richer than the phosphor at its centre. The multiplier goes up (glow 1.15) because emerald carries a third of the mint's luminance, so the net light is 24-29% lower but reads as depth. It covers the key word, Send's ring and pool, the mark's tile, live lights, the box's focus and the greeting's pool. The tube glass takes an emerald breath too (screen-glass #04120c).

caveats: Interaction and usability found the caps tiles harder to read than rows ('Set the Status tiles as sentence-case rows with lamps'), and system found that 'the lit plates fill surfaces with green'. Set the legends in sentence case, lower the lit fill so only the lamp bar and the legend glow, and keep a 44px minimum height. The sheet's comment promised a 'dark cockpit' (normal stays dark), which is not what shipped. It is Flight Console's own device; it is listed for the other lineages too.
suits: console: its own annunciator, to be made readable. track: a signal box's panel of route windows, lit when a route is set. switchboard: the Status cell's sub-cells as annunciator windows. figure: Status's figure.

feature: Hand-drawn loop for 'here'
what: The current place is circled as if by hand: in the bar, on the phone's tab strip, in the Settings nav and the menu. The loop is one open, slightly overshooting SVG path with a tail, stretched over the link as a background. It is drawn with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke, so the line stays 2.4px at any size. Today on the month is circled the same way.

Under it the tally is set large: '● 6 working ○ 7 off' in condensed tabular figures. The whole house's state reads in one glance, before any list.

feature: State marks as inked rubber stamps

'NEEDS A LOOK' on Settings reads as an inspector's mark.

The pulse is brass on ordinary days and lit green with bloom on today, drawn as a mask of pulse.svg, so the eye finds busy days before reading.

feature: Four shapes, four jobs, with their key in the footer
what: One rule for every page: the circle is light (tubes, lamps, the mark, today), the square is the family's (cards, fields, ticks, faces), the bar is the page's own structure (the poster's base, section heads, the current place, buttons), and the triangle is what needs a look (late tasks carry a small amber triangle before 'was due'). Corners are square and only light is round. Every footer closes with a legend of the four: a lit dot 'LIGHT', a square 'YOURS', a bar 'THE PAGE', a triangle 'A LOOK'.

feature: Serif for the one question and the page titles
what: 'What's on your mind?' is set in Newsreader, a bookish optical-size serif, with the green 'mind' glowing in it. Page titles and section heads use the same serif at optical sizes 60 and 30, with oldstyle figures in the heads and tabular lining figures kept for data. Beside DM Sans text and DM Mono small print, this gives a four-step hierarchy: serif for what is titled, sans for what is read, mono for the machine, VT323 for glass.

feature: Book measure for prose
what: Prose is held to a book measure whatever the layout. Ledes are 1.22rem/1.45 at weight 380 and capped at 34em. Running text in plates, source notes, hints and descriptions is capped at 32em (about 75 characters), and chat lines at 36em. p and li use text-wrap: pretty with hyphens: auto, headings use text-wrap: balance, and the time-zone note is pulled up into the lede's size.

Type's notes: "Porcelain Atlas proves the owner's taste for typesetting can be served by measure and leading without a serif body; graft its measure discipline for prose (ledes, help text, Vera's replies at 60-62ch), not its serif controls."

feature: Type features keyed to who is speaking, a slashed zero and a written scale
what: One custom property, --ot, feeds font-feature-settings and is set by role. The family's words (Plex Sans) take "ss01","ss02", the schoolbook single-storey a and g. Everything the machine reports (mono facts, times, counts, legends, tabs, said-by lines, data tables) takes "zero", a slashed zero like an IBM terminal. Every size sits on a major-third scale written as tokens: --t-1 .8, --t0 1, --t1 1.25, --t2 1.5625, --t3 1.953, --t4 2.441rem, and --t6 3.815rem for the tubes' big figures only. It replaced about forty sizes.

feature: EFIS colour code: one meaning per colour
what: Every colour has one meaning on every page, after the 1982 EFIS glass-cockpit code (itself drawn on a CRT). #6dff9c means active or live: the mark, Send, 'mind', focus, live lamps, the tubes and the NOW box. Sage means on or done. Cyan #83bfec means selected or entered by the family: links, the 1.5px selection box for 'here', family names in label lines, the edge of their chat lines and their initials. Bone is for legends, titles and data, and neutral grey for labels and computed data. Amber means caution only and red warning or off only; there is no magenta. The code is written at the top of the sheet.

Flight Console: data-entry wells, a calm version of the glass cockpit's 'cyan entered' code. Figure Ground: its form plates and Settings figures, where the lit field is the figure's subject. Works as the control material in all six lineages, on the To do and Settings pages above all.

feature: 44px hit area around a small tick box, with no layout change
what: Checkboxes and radios keep a 1.15rem visible well but get a full 44px hit area without moving anything. The input is appearance:none and sized calc(1.15rem + 26px) with a 13px transparent border and -13px margins. The well is painted with a padding-box background, its edge is an inset shadow, and the focus ring is pulled in (outline-offset -11px) to hug the visible box. The tick scales in over .12s. The result was 0 of 56 small targets on Home and 0 of 97 on To do.

feature: Lines only where there is a sequence: setup stations and the fallback chain
what: Lines are drawn only where the data has an order. 'Finish setting up' hangs its steps on a vertical amber line that drops from an amber ring round its icon, with a hollow amber stop per step. feature: The P7 flash: violet on arrival, green afterglow
what: The companion colour is justified as phosphor light itself. A radar's P7 tube lit each echo with a brief blue-violet flash, and a long green afterglow stayed on after it. In the palette the flash appears as an indigo-violet light in the greeting (#7d68ff at washGlow 2.6, clean at (34,34,56)), an afterglow under every bar (#7270f8 at topGlow 2.0), violet links and pill (#aea3fd), and a deep on-hue green halo (#2eac66). The device worth taking is the sequence: whatever is new arrives violet-white and decays to the steady green.

feature: Newspaper column rules between Status's open columns
what: On Status, the three panels (Who answers, Keys, Connected to) lose their boxes and are set as open columns under thick-and-thin head rules. A 1px vertical column rule sits in the middle of each 2.5rem gutter, from the head rule's foot to the last item, as in a newspaper. The rule appears only at 72rem and wider, so a wrapped column never draws a stray line. The page reads as a set page of three stories, not three cards.

praise: Type 8.0: 'Status has column rules'. Feedback 6.5: 'open ruled columns on Status'. Soul 7.6: Status 'as ruled columns'. Skeptic 5.9: 'ruled Status columns. It changes structure rather than tint.' Style 7.3: 'Coming up, To do and Status sit open on the black, which gives the green-on-black signature more room'. Type fix: add a hairline between columns where they wrap below 72rem. System fix: show the column rule from 52rem.

suits: timetable: a timetable is columns under rules, so column rules between time, what and who, and between days, turn the chat-as-timetable into a real printed timetable. figure: figures set side by side as stat columns separated by column rules, like a newspaper's box score. console: the instrument columns of the annunciator and crew board.

feature: Portrait 404 tube beside its words

It stands on the left of a slate tray at about 19rem, and on the right sit the eyebrow 'Nothing on the radar', 'Not found', the line and 'Back to the start', centred on the monitor. The monitor stops dominating the page and becomes an instrument beside its message.

feature: Sign in and 404 as the two ends of a line
what: On desktop the monitor stands on the left (22rem) and the words sit on the right, on a short vertical track. On Sign in the track starts at an accent terminus ring beside the title, and a phosphor ring with a small bloom sits on the track level with the password field: 'you are here, waiting for you'. The button is the end of the line. On the 404 the same short track runs past 'Not found' and ends at a buffer stop (a 14x2px bar) beside 'Back to the start': the end of the line.

feature: Home as an open book with a shaded gutter
what: Below the greeting, Home is a two-page spread. The left page (verso) holds time: Coming up, then To do. The right page (recto) holds what the family keeps: Lately added, Something to eat, the kids' wishes. A single 1px gutter rule runs down the centre, with a wide soft black shadow (28px, 7px spread) that makes it read as the fold of a book. There is a 4.5rem column gap.

feature: Window legend set into the frame line
what: Every read section is a flat steel field (#171d20) with a 1px frame drawn .6rem inside it by ::before. Its heading is set into the top line after a 1.25rem stub, with the section icon in its section colour, the only place the section colour appears. The way on ('All plans ->', 'All 4', 'Add an idea / All 12', 'Change a key') is moved after its list and set into the bottom-right line. Tabs (All ideas | Restaurants, List | Month) become the window's legend, with the current tab in reverse video. Any generic .panel becomes a window, so Family, Memory, Restaurants and the idea pages inherit it with no markup of their own. It is period grammar carried by line, not by paint.

feature: Head bracket that gathers a page's controls
what: Each page head starts at a ring round the page's icon, drawn 1.5px in the page's colour with a faint glow. When the head holds controls, a 1px pewter bracket drops from the ring, turns one 12px corner and runs under them. On Ideas it gathers the tabs, 'Save a thought' and 'Add an idea' into one bracketed row; on To do, the Add fold, Show, Search and Filter. A head with nothing to hold ends in a 14x3 buffer stop. DOM and Tab order are unchanged.

feature: Double frame for what you act in, lit while you type
what: The line weight carries meaning. What you read is a single-frame window. What you act in (the ask box, the filters, forms, Settings groups, pickers, the bar menu) is a #1b2126 dialog in a 3px double frame (#4c5760). A form's heading sits on the double line on a 4px band of the outside colour. While a text field, textarea or select inside is focused, the whole double frame turns lit sage (#86d9a6), but not on button focus, so the form you are in lights up as one unit.

what: On Status each lamp sits in a 2.25rem designator cell at the left of its row. The cell takes an 8% wash of the lit colour only while the lamp is on. An 'on' row reads as a lit cell and an 'off' row as a dark cell with a hollow ring, so the state survives a squint without any more glow.

feature: Section cursor tick (the mark's block cursor, in each section's colour)

It is set through a --tick custom property on the section. A head that already has an icon gets no tick, only a proper gap after the icon. Two round-4 heirs sharpen it. That rule holds on Plans' month head, Settings groups and the Status panels.

Feedback fix: 'Keep the section ticks; they are the palette's best variation device'. The skeptic asked to breed them into Navy Room. For Slate Console's version, interaction 7.3: 'A sage cursor marks the start of every section ... the best scanning aid here'. Round-4 type lens: 'Plum Ink: the gift-icon gap and section ticks' are worth breeding.
caveats: Soul 6.0: 'the multicoloured section ticks lean to confetti'. Round-4 lessons: 'Cursors are the new confetti risk'. Round 5 says the same of coloured rule leads: keep colour on Coming up and Lately added only and give the rest pewter #47535b. Style asked for a 3px rounded bar so it reads as a mark and not a bullet. The system lens asked for one heading marker per head, never an icon and a tick side by side. Keep it solid. Let it glow only when it marks something live, since a glowing block after a title read as an editable caret (Composing Room). Its main-line heirs are the 2px section cap and the coloured rule lead, so bring the cursor shape back, not a second colour device.
suits: switchboard: each page cell's key opens with this block in its page's colour, a direct echo of the mark's FamilyDB▮, lit (with halo) only on a cell whose page has something new or live. figure: the tick sits before each figure's small-caps label in the figure's colour, tying the number to its section. pocket: NOW, NEXT and LATER heads carry the cursor, lit at NOW, solid at NEXT and pewter at LATER, so brightness says how near. track and timetable need it less, since their lamps already do this job.

feature: Legend set into the frame line
standing: 7.31, #2 of 12 in round 5 (6.67, #3 of 12 in round 6)
what: Each group is a 1px silk-screened outline, and its head is a condensed, tracked caps legend cut into the outline's top line, the way a fieldset legend or a bench instrument's panel print sits. The icon is tinted in the section's colour, and the 'All plans' or 'Earlier / Later' keys sit in the same line at the right. The legend row is 44px tall and pulled up by calc(-1.375rem - 0.5px) so the line runs through its middle; each child sits on a patch of ground colour that breaks the line. On Plans the month is one framed group with SEPTEMBER 2026 and its keys in the frame; on Status the three columns are framed groups with WHO ANSWERS, KEYS and CONNECTED TO as legends.

praise: Type lens, round 5, 7.1: 'The best new typographic device of the round: condensed, tracked caps legends set into the frame line, like fieldset legends silk-screened on a panel.' Type lens, round 6, 7.0: 'the most period-true typographic device here, and they hold on every page … Keep the legends exactly as they are; they are the trait to breed.' caveats: The patch is painted var(--bg), so it shows as a black blot on any slate or glass ground: use a `--legend-bg` token set on each container (system fix). The caps shouted over card titles: drop to about .9rem/600, and the round 10 rule says a legend never ranks below the rows it governs, and links in the line stay sentence case. The groups were empty outlines on bare black, which drained Status: put a slate fill inside the frame. The main line carried rail legends in rounds 8-9 (Reverse Video, Signal Legend), but today's leaders (Desk Terminal) do not.
suits: Flight Console: the console bays' engraved legends cut into each bay's frame, with the readouts' keys in the same line. Videotex Switchboard: each page cell's number and name set into its frame, like a patch-panel legend, with the count at the right of the line. Figure Ground: the plate number and title in the plate's frame above its figure. Night Timetable: each timetable's line sign cut into its frame.

feature: Label-over-data rows
what: Each row is set as a flight computer's line pair. A designator comes first (a date leaf, a tick or a kind icon). Then a small label line in grey condensed mono caps ('THURSDAY 1 OCTOBER, 10:00', 'ACTIVITY FOR MAYA, THEO') sits over the data line in bone sans 600 at 1rem ('Silver Falls hike'). A fixed tabular facts column at the right reads straight down ('in 2 days'). Late tasks split into two amber lines, 'was due' over '2 days ago'.
